briefing.opening: Good day. We now begin the Climate Change Daily Briefing for November 20, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 KMA's New Climate Scenarios: Warning of a 3.6°C Rise by Century's End Under High Emissions
sections.content: The Korea Meteorological Administration (KMA) has calculated and released its first global climate change scenarios for the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) Seventh Assessment cycle [10, 15]. The analysis revealed that if greenhouse gas emissions are not effectively curtailed, global average temperatures will rise by 3.6°C in the late 21st century, with East Asia surging by up to 3.8°C [2, 4, 16]. The new scientific evidence presented by the research team clearly indicates that avoiding a global climate catastrophe will be nearly impossible if emissions reductions are delayed [1, 3, 19].

sections.title: 🌍 COP31 in Deadlock: Pushed into Overtime Amid Omission of Fossil Fuel Phaseout and Finance Clashes
sections.content: The 31st UN Climate Change Conference (COP31), held in Antalya, Türkiye, has been pushed into overtime amid intense backlash following the omission of fossil fuel-related commitments from the draft agreement [141, 154, 177]. Tensions escalated as developed nations insisted on prioritizing existing pledges over African nations' calls for additional climate finance, while the divide between oil-producing nations seeking drilling expansion and low-lying Pacific island nations facing existential threats remained unbridged [142, 176, 178, 179]. Denouncing this summit as a 'COP of Betrayal' for failing to include a fossil fuel phaseout and concrete financial mechanisms, civil society groups and key participant nations are demanding a strong agreement [7, 161, 165].

sections.title: ⚠️ IEA Warning: Reversal in Power Consumption Patterns and South Korea's High Energy Import Dependence
sections.content: According to the International Energy Agency (IEA), global warming is deepening a structural shift in global energy consumption, with demand increasingly skewing toward cooling rather than heating [6]. Compounding this, the proliferation of AI and data centers is projected to drive a 13-fold surge in electricity demand by 2060 and a 70% increase in associated carbon emissions by 2030, adding further strain to power grids [91, 138]. Highlighting South Korea's critical vulnerability—with 80% of its energy demand reliant on imports—the IEA advised the active implementation of its 100GW renewable energy deployment target to mitigate supply chain risks and curb emissions [83, 97, 100, 120].

sections.title: 🌱 Locally Driven Carbon Neutrality: Securing National Funding and Advancing Renewable Infrastructure
sections.content: Substantive policy execution for climate crisis response and energy transition is accelerating across local governments in South Korea [22, 57]. The Jeonnam-Gwangju region secured 27.5 billion KRW in national funding—the largest in the country—to deploy renewable energy across 11,300 sites next year [87, 95, 126]. In addition, field-centered climate actions are gaining momentum: Osan City is supplying solar power from public parking lots to local businesses to support RE100, while municipalities such as Siheung and Sangju have been awarded ministerial honors for outstanding carbon neutrality initiatives driven by civic engagement and resource circulation [22, 27, 75, 129].

briefing.closing: Even amid the deadlock in global climate negotiations, scientific warnings and local implementation on the ground are becoming increasingly clear. That concludes today's climate briefing.
